title: A Promise for the Songbook
premise: Mirabel Okafor, once the most sought-after wedding planner in the city, now runs a failing events business and refuses to attend the ceremonies he still designs, haunted by the fiancée who left him at his own rehearsal dinner ten years ago. For a decade, an anonymous correspondent has slipped letters into his late grandmother's songbook—letters he assumed were hers, until Theo Lindqvist, the quiet new neighbor, turns out to be their author: the boy who witnessed the abandonment and has been writing apologies on behalf of everyone who failed Mirabel, including himself. As Mirabel plans one last wedding that could save his business, he and Theo fall into a fragile intimacy threatened by the truth that Theo's family's inheritance dispute is what drove the betrayal that ruined Mirabel's engagement. At the wedding itself, Mirabel must choose between exposing the injustice for revenge or letting justice take a quieter form—returning the songbook, with its final letter, to the family it was stolen from—and forgiving himself enough to stand at the altar of his own second chance.
about_author: August Halloran is the pen name of a former estate lawyer who left practice to write love stories about people the legal system failed. He lives above a bookbindery, where he claims all his best endings are stitched by hand.

chapters.title: The Planner Who Doesn't Dance
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He orchestrates a flawless wedding from the loading dock, never entering the ballroom, then returns home to find a moving truck next door and a man struggling with a piano. The beat is controlled loneliness cracking slightly at an unexpected kindness.

chapters.title: Letters in the Margins
chapters.summary: Mirabel rereads the songbook his grandmother left him, noticing for the first time that the marginalia spans years beyond her death. A new letter appears, postmarked this week. The emotional beat is vertigo—the past rewriting itself in real time.

chapters.title: The Neighbor with the Piano
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He unpacks his late mother's belongings, hiding a folder of unsent drafts, and recognizes Mirabel from a photograph inside the songbook he returned to the Okafor mailbox years ago. The beat is guilty longing disguised as neighborliness.

chapters.title: One Last Contract
chapters.summary: Mirabel takes the commission that could save his business: the Whitmore-Hale wedding, hosted by the family whose name he's spent a decade avoiding. Theo offers to help as a favor. The beat is dread wearing the mask of ambition.

chapters.title: What the Songbook Was For
chapters.summary: Theo confesses nothing but reveals much: the songbook belonged to his grandmother first, traded away during an inheritance settlement that cheated his mother out of the family estate. The beat is grief finding a witness.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinners and Other Lies
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Wedding planning forces him and Theo into late nights; a near-kiss is interrupted when Mirabel realizes the Whitmores were present at his abandoned rehearsal dinner—and that Theo's surname connects to them. The beat is desire curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Author, Unmasked
chapters.summary: Confrontation in Theo's apartment: Mirabel finds the drafts and learns Theo watched the abandonment, wrote every letter, and moved here deliberately to earn forgiveness before the estate lawsuit closes forever. The beat is betrayal layered over tenderness.

chapters.title: Justice Has No Courtroom
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Rather than fight the Whitmores in court, Theo prepares to sign away his claim, believing he deserves nothing—not the house, not Mirabel. The beat is self-punishment mistaken for penance.

chapters.title: The Wedding
chapters.summary: Climax. During the ceremony, Mirabel publicly returns the songbook to Theo, naming the theft and the letters aloud—justice rendered outside any law—and walks out mid-reception, finally entering a wedding instead of hiding from one. The beat is rupture as liberation.

chapters.title: A Promise for the Songbook
chapters.summary: Resolution. Weeks later, Theo writes one final letter and delivers it by hand; Mirabel answers with a contract of his own—a promise, co-signed, to stop planning other people's beginnings and start his own. The beat is forgiveness, of the mirror first.
